## The goal

On January 7, 2025, the Palisades and Eaton fires ignited in Los Angeles
County. How bad did the air get, at one monitor downtown, that winter?

You answer with six numbers, written to a file called `results.csv`.

## The six numbers

Your window is **December 1, 2024 through February 28, 2025**, at EPA site
`06-037-1103` ("Los Angeles-North Main Street"), primary regulatory monitor
only.

| `quantity` | what it is | format |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `peak_pm25` | The highest daily PM2.5 reading in the window | 1 decimal, e.g. `47.3` |
| `peak_date` | The day that peak fell on | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `jan_mean` | Mean of the January 2025 readings | 2 decimals |
| `days_above_35` | Days strictly above 35 µg/m³ | whole number |
| `missing_days` | Calendar days in the window with no reading at all | whole number |
| `peak_over_dec_mean` | `peak_pm25` divided by the December 2024 mean | 2 decimals |

`results.csv` has exactly two columns, `quantity` and `value`, and exactly
those six rows in that order. `results_spec.md` in your starter is the full
contract, and the grader reads the file against it.

PM2.5 is fine particulate matter, in micrograms per cubic meter (µg/m³).
EPA's 24-hour health standard is 35 µg/m³.

## Do this one without AI {#no-ai}

The syllabus permits AI tools on homework by default. **This assignment is
an exception**, and it is the only kind of exception the course makes: an
assignment where the whole point is the vocabulary.

Everything you need is on the [R essentials](../sessions/02-r-essentials.qmd)
page. Every function, every repair, every check. If you hand this to a
chatbot it will produce six correct numbers in about nine seconds, and you
will have learned nothing that the rest of the semester depends on. You
cannot verify a model's work in a language you do not read, and verifying is
what this course is for.

Ask a classmate. Ask in office hours. Re-run the session script until the
pieces stick. Then write it yourself.

## The data

Two CSVs in `data/`, exactly as EPA's download tool ships them. Nothing has
been cleaned, sorted, or reformatted. `data/SOURCE.md` records the source
URL, the exact download selections, and file checksums, so you can
re-download and compare.

Two things about the files that are not mistakes:

- **You get two files.** EPA's tool downloads one calendar year at a time,
  and your window crosses the year boundary. The columns are identical.
- **The site runs five instruments.** A site is a place; a monitor is one
  instrument at that place. Keep all five and you get up to five rows for
  the same day. The assignment tells you which one to keep.

`read.csv()` also damages two columns on the way in, silently. Catching that
is part of the work.

## Reference checkpoints

The expected values are disclosed on purpose. The pipeline from raw file to
answer is the assignment; the numbers were never the secret.

- EPA's 24-hour PM2.5 standard is 35 µg/m³.
- The file carries EPA's own Air Quality Index in `Daily AQI Value`. On the
  peak day it reads 182, which EPA labels "Unhealthy".
- Four `stopifnot()` checks in `hw1.R` gate the stages. Uncomment each as
  you reach it. **Editing a check so it passes scores worse than leaving it
  failing honestly.**

## What to submit

Two files, due Thursday, September 3, 8:40 am:

- `hw1.R` — your edited script
- `results.csv` — written by that script

Open your private repo in the course GitHub organization, drag both files
onto the repo page, and commit. No git client needed.

Before you upload, restart R and source your script from scratch. It must
run top to bottom in a fresh session with no errors. The grader runs it
exactly that way.

## Weighting

| Dimension | Points | The question it asks |
|:--|--:|:--|
| Reproduces | 15 | Does the script run, start to finish, in a fresh session? |
| Correct | 60 | Are the six numbers right, and does your script compute them? |
| Verified | 15 | Did you check your own work? |
| Craft | 10 | Can someone else read it? |

The question points inside `hw1.R` sum to 100 and scale by 0.6 into Correct.
A `results.csv` with the right numbers and a script that does not compute
them scores 0 on Correct. The full rubric ships in your starter as
`rubric.md`; the course-wide scheme is in the
[syllabus](../syllabus.qmd#homework).
